What is Base64?
Base64 is an encoding scheme that converts binary data into ASCII text using 64 safe characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, /).
Why use Base64 encoding?
Base64 allows binary data to safely transmit over text-based channels like email, HTTP headers, and JSON APIs.
Is Base64 encryption?
No. Base64 is encoding (reversible), not encryption (secure, key-based). It offers no security.
Can I decode Base64?
Yes. Base64 is fully reversible. Any Base64 string can be decoded back to original data.
What does the = character mean in Base64?
The = character is padding used to make Base64 output length a multiple of 4.
How much does Base64 increase file size?
Base64 increases size by approximately 33% (3 bytes become 4 characters).
Can I use Base64 for images?
Yes. Images can be Base64-encoded for embedding in HTML or CSS as data URLs.
What is a data URL?
A data URL embeds Base64-encoded content directly in HTML using the data: protocol (data:image/png;base64,...).
Should I use Base64 for all images?
No. Data URLs increase HTML size significantly. Use for small images or when embedding is necessary.
Is Base64 the only encoding?
No. Other encodings include URL encoding, hexadecimal, and base32. Choose based on use case.
What are the limitations of Base64?
Limited to safe ASCII characters, increases file size by 33%, and offers no security or compression.
Can Base64 be used for passwords?
No. Never use Base64 for passwords. Use proper password hashing (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2).
